issue.title: Issue: prevent a agent from exceeding the token limit
issue.body:
### Issue you'd like to raise.

Hey there, I'm trying got find a way to prevent an agent from going over the token limit, I've looked at the docs, asked around and had no luck.

This is the error for better content:
 [ERROR] InvalidRequestError: This model's maximum context length is 16384 tokens. However, your messages resulted in 17822 tokens. Please reduce the length of the messages.

Any help would be great 😊

<!-- Answer -->
Hello,

Thank you for reaching out. The error you're encountering is due to the total number of tokens in your messages exceeding the model's maximum context length. In LangChain, you can manage this by setting the `max_tokens` attribute of the `OpenAI` class to a specific value that is within the model's maximum context length.

Here's an example of how you can set the `max_tokens` attribute:

```python
from langchain.llms import OpenAI

# Create an instance of the OpenAI class
openai = OpenAI(model_name="text-davinci-003")

# Get the maximum context size for the model
max_context_size = openai.modelname_to_contextsize(openai.model_name)

# Set the max_tokens attribute to a value within the model's maximum context length
openai.max_tokens = max_context_size - 1  # or any value less than max_context_size

# Alternatively, you can use the max_tokens_for_prompt method
prompt = "Tell me a joke."
openai.max_tokens = openai.max_tokens_for_prompt(prompt)
```

This will ensure that the number of tokens generated by the model does not exceed the model's maximum context length, thus preventing the InvalidRequestError.

You can also refer to these similar issues for more context:
- [Issue #2333](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/2333)
- [Issue #3670](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/3670)
- [Issue #5237](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/5237)

Please note that the default value of `max_tokens` in the `OpenAI` class is 256. If you're frequently encountering this error, you might want to consider setting `max_tokens` to a lower value.

I hope this helps! If you have any other questions, feel free to ask.

Best,
Dosu

Hello,

You're on the right track with managing the token limit error by setting the `max_tokens` attribute of the `OpenAI` class to a value within the model's maximum context length. This is a common approach to ensure that the number of tokens generated does not exceed the model's maximum context length.

Your usage of the `modelname_to_contextsize` method is correct. This method is designed to dynamically determine the maximum context size for a given model, which can be more efficient if you're working with different models and don't want to manually set `max_tokens` each time.

```python
openai = OpenAI(model_name="text-davinci-003")
openai.max_tokens = openai.modelname_to_contextsize(openai.model_name)
```

The `max_tokens_for_prompt` method you're using is also a good approach. It calculates the maximum number of tokens possible to generate for a specific prompt, allowing you to dynamically adjust the `max_tokens` based on the length of the input prompt.

```python
openai = OpenAI(model_name="text-davinci-003")
prompt = "Tell me a joke."
openai.max_tokens = openai.max_tokens_for_prompt(prompt)
```

Regarding the default value of `max_tokens`, it is indeed set to 256 in the `OpenAI` class. This parameter sets the maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion. If `max_tokens` is set to -1, it returns as many tokens as possible given the prompt and the model's maximal context size. If the number of tokens generated exceeds the `max_tokens` value, a token limit error will be raised.

```python
max_tokens: int = 256
"""The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion.
-1 returns as many tokens as possible given the prompt and
the models maximal context size."""
```

Setting `max_tokens` to a lower value could help avoid the token limit error, but it might also limit the amount of information returned by the model. It's a balance you'll need to find based on your specific use case.
